ThirdDerivativeBounded s f := Differentiable f and Differentiable (fderiv f) and Differentiable (iteratedFDeriv 2 f) and forall W U V X, |iteratedFDeriv 3 f W ![U,V,X]| <= s ||U|| ||V|| ||X||. Equivalence with the run-1 (accepted) fderiv-nested form and with the source: by Mathlib's iteratedFDeriv_succ_apply_left, iteratedFDeriv (k+1) f W (m) = fderiv (iteratedFDeriv k f) W (m 0) (tail m), and iteratedFDeriv 1 f = (continuousMultilinearCurryFin1).symm o fderiv f, iteratedFDeriv 2 f = curry-equiv o fderiv (fderiv f) (composition with linear isometric equivalences commutes with fderiv and preserves differentiability). Hence iteratedFDeriv 2 f W ![U,V] = D^2 f(W)[U][V], iteratedFDeriv 3 f W ![U,V,X] = D^3 f(W)[U][V][X], and Differentiable (iteratedFDeriv 2 f) <-> Differentiable (fderiv (fderiv f)). So the definition says: f is three times differentiable and the trilinear third derivative satisfies |D^3 f(W)[U,V,X]| <= s ||U||_F ||V||_F ||X||_F for all arguments, i.e. ||nabla^3 f_v(w)||_op <= s with the tensor operator norm of line 143 (vec is an isometry; bound over all U,V,X so the argument order is irrelevant). Exactly Assumption 4.7 with its presupposed differentiability; equivalent to the run-1 definition; nothing stronger (no continuity of the third derivative).
